misconceptions.claim: A fluid flowing at a steady rate has no acceleration.
misconceptions.correction: A change in speed or direction is an acceleration, so the fluid is accelerating even at a steady rate.

summary: Flow rate Q is defined to be the volume V flowing past a point in time t, or Q=Vt where V is volume and t is time.
The SI unit of volume is m3.
Another common unit is the liter (L), which is 10−3m3.

misconceptions.claim: A fast-moving fluid always has a higher pressure than a slow-moving one.
misconceptions.correction: For steady horizontal flow at constant height, Bernoulli’s equation gives a lower pressure where the speed is higher. The pressure difference is what accelerates the fluid.
misconceptions.signal: The pressure is lower where the fluid speeds up, not higher.

misconceptions.claim: Bernoulli’s equation applies to any flow, including turbulent flow.
misconceptions.correction: It applies along a streamline in steady, incompressible, nonviscous flow. Turbulent flow has eddies and energy losses that the simple equation does not describe.
misconceptions.signal: The equation comes from energy conservation under restrictive assumptions.

sections.title: Viscosity and Laminar Flow; Poiseuille’s Law
objectives: Define laminar flow and turbulent flow.
Explain what viscosity is.
Calculate flow and resistance with Poiseuille’s law.

misconceptions.claim: Viscosity and density are the same property of a fluid.
misconceptions.correction: Density is mass per unit volume. Viscosity is the fluid’s resistance to flow, or its internal friction. Oil is less dense than water but much more viscous.
misconceptions.signal: A fluid can be dense and runny, or light and thick.

misconceptions.claim: A more viscous fluid always flows faster in a pipe.
misconceptions.correction: For the same pressure difference, a more viscous fluid flows more slowly. Poiseuille’s law puts viscosity in the denominator.
misconceptions.signal: Viscosity resists flow, so it cannot increase the flow rate.

summary: Laminar flow is characterized by smooth flow of the fluid in layers that do not mix.
Turbulence is characterized by eddies and swirls that mix layers of fluid together.
Fluid viscosity η is due to friction within a fluid. Representative values are given in . Viscosity has units of ( N/m 2 ) s or Pa ⋅ s .

sections.title: The Onset of Turbulence
objectives: Calculate Reynolds number.
Use the Reynolds number for a system to determine whether it is laminar or turbulent.

misconceptions.claim: Turbulence begins at one fixed speed for every pipe and fluid.
misconceptions.correction: The onset depends on the Reynolds number, which combines speed, size, density and viscosity. Geometry also matters.
misconceptions.signal: The same speed can be laminar in a wide pipe and turbulent in a narrow one.

summary: The Reynolds number NR can reveal whether flow is laminar or turbulent. It isNR=2ρvrη.
For NR below about 2000, flow is laminar. For NR above about 3000, flow is turbulent. For values of NR between 2000 and 3000, it may be either or both.

sections.title: Motion of an Object in a Viscous Fluid
objectives: Calculate the Reynolds number for an object moving through a fluid.
Explain whether the Reynolds number indicates laminar or turbulent flow.
Describe the conditions under which an object has a terminal speed.

misconceptions.claim: An object falling through a fluid keeps accelerating until it lands.
misconceptions.correction: Drag grows with speed. When drag plus buoyancy balances the weight, the net force is zero and the object falls at its terminal speed.
misconceptions.signal: Terminal speed is a steady state, not a pause.

misconceptions.claim: Terminal speed depends only on the object’s weight.
misconceptions.correction: It also depends on the object’s size and shape and on the fluid’s density and viscosity. A flat sheet falls more slowly than a compact sphere of the same weight.
misconceptions.signal: Two objects of equal weight can have very different terminal speeds.

summary: When an object moves in a fluid, there is a different form of the Reynolds number NR′=ρvLη(object in fluid), which indicates whether flow is laminar or turbulent.
For NR′ less than about one, flow is laminar.
For NR′ greater than 106, flow is entirely turbulent.

authored_exercises.stem: What is meant by the terminal speed of an object falling through a fluid?
authored_exercises.answer: The constant speed reached when the drag and buoyancy forces balance the object’s weight, so the net force is zero.
solution: When drag plus buoyancy equals weight, the net force is zero.
The object then falls at a constant terminal speed.

authored_exercises.stem: A sphere falls through oil at its terminal speed of 0.2 m/s. What is its acceleration at that instant?
solution: Terminal speed means the speed is constant.

authored_exercises.stem: A small sphere of radius 0.5 mm and density 7800 kg/m³ falls through oil of density 900 kg/m³ and viscosity 0.5 Pa s. Estimate its terminal speed using Stokes’ law. Take g = 9.8 m/s².

sections.title: Molecular Transport Phenomena: Diffusion, Osmosis, and Related Processes
objectives: Define diffusion, osmosis, dialysis, and active transport.
Calculate diffusion rates.

misconceptions.claim: Diffusion needs a pump or stirring to move molecules through a fluid.
misconceptions.correction: Diffusion is driven by random thermal motion. A concentration difference makes the net movement directional, but no pump is needed.
misconceptions.signal: Molecular motion is always present, even in still fluid.

misconceptions.claim: Osmosis is simply the diffusion of solute particles through a membrane.
misconceptions.correction: Osmosis is the movement of solvent through a semipermeable membrane from a less concentrated to a more concentrated solution. The solute may be unable to cross.
misconceptions.signal: It is the solvent that moves in osmosis.

summary: Diffusion is the movement of substances due to random thermal molecular motion.
The average distance xrms a molecule travels by diffusion in a given amount of time is given byxrms=2Dt,where D is the diffusion constant, representative values of which are found in .

Osmosis is a process by which molecules of a solvent pass through a semipermeable membrane from a less concentrated solution into a more concentrated one, thus, equalizing the solute concentrations on each side of the membrane.

authored_exercises.stem: A molecule has diffusion constant 2.0 × 10^-9 m²/s. Find its root-mean-square diffusion distance in 100 s.

At the gorge, the river narrows to 20 m wide and averages 20 m deep. (a) What is the average speed of the river in the gorge? (b) What is the average speed of the water in the river downstream of the falls when it widens to 60 m and its depth increases to an average of 40 m?
